description: INV-1 NO-HUMAN CHECK STILL RUNS ON COMMENT-STRIPPED SOURCE — sprint-1 FIND-008(b) NOT FIXED. test-deploy-akash.sh:9 strips ALL comments (`src="$(sed 's/#.*//' "$S")"`) and the INV-1 absent-check at line 16 (`absent "console-api|credit card|managed wallet"`) greps that STRIPPED source. The no-human guarantee is the security-critical invariant of this whole feature (spec INV-1), yet a `console-api.akash.network` URL or 'managed wallet' reference smuggled into deploy-akash.sh behind a `#` (or on a comment line, e.g. `curl https://console-api.akash.network/... # fallback`) would be erased by the strip BEFORE the absent-grep runs, so the oracle would PASS while a Console/credit-card path was present. Comment-stripping is correct for the presence/order INV-2 checks, but the no-human ABSENCE check must scan the RAW file. This makes the strongest invariant gameable.

evidence.snippet:
src="$(sed 's/#.*//' "$S")"           # comments stripped
...
absent "console-api|credit card|managed wallet"  "INV-1 no-human: NO Console/credit-card path"

correctFix: Run the INV-1 no-human absent-check against the RAW file contents (the unstripped `$S`), e.g. `grep -qiE 'console-api|credit card|managed wallet' "$S" && fail`. Keep comment-stripping only for the INV-2 presence/order greps. Also prefer full-line-comment removal (`grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#'`) over `s/#.*//` which clobbers inline `#` in any future active code.
